query: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloys are promising bond-coat candidates because of their mechanical properties and elevated-temperature oxidation resistance. Earlier HVAF-M3 work identified 15–45 μm feedstock as optimal for high-quality coatings, but applying the same composition and size range with the HVAF-i7 torch yielded acceptable coating quality yet inadequate thickness. Separate studies of conventional MCrAlY bond coats using the M3 system reported a slight gain in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocity and nozzle-specific best spray distances of 300 and 350 mm. The design target is a sufficiently thick, adherent bond coat that retains coating integrity, minimal as-sprayed oxidation, and durability during high-temperature thermal-barrier service, including deposition within internal diameters as small as 120 mm. What single intervention could overcome the thickness limitation? State the hypothesized intervention and mechanism, predict the outcome relative to the 15–45 μm-feedstock baseline, define the deposition and service conditions under which it should remain effective, identify supporting evidence from the cited prior studies, and propose a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the HVAF-i7 spray distance to achieve higher in-flight particle velocity will improve deposition efficiency, yielding thicker FeCoNiCrAl coatings with maintained adhesion and minimal oxidation.
generation.material_initial_state: FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy feedstock with 15–45 μm particle size used for bond coat deposition.
generation.intervention: Adjust HVAF-i7 parameters by reducing the spray stand‐off distance to approximately 300–350 mm to increase particle velocity during deposition.
generation.conditions: Deposition for bond coats in internal diameters as small as 120 mm intended for high‐temperature thermal-barrier service.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced particle kinetic energy promotes stronger particle impingement (splatting), leading to increased particle-to-substrate bonding and reduced in-flight oxidation.
generation.mechanism: Shortening the spray distance increases particle velocity so that the particles retain higher kinetic energy as they impact the substrate. This yields a thicker, more adherent coating by both enhancing splat formation and reducing oxidation time in flight.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline 15–45 μm feedstock deposition using standard HVAF-i7 parameters (which resulted in acceptable quality but insufficient thickness), the intervention is expected to significantly increase coating thickness, while maintaining coating integrity, low as-sprayed oxidation, and durability under high-temperature conditions.
generation.baseline: Prior HVAF-M3 work with 15–45 μm feedstock achieved high-quality bond coats and conventional MCrAlY studies indicated slight gains in deposition efficiency at higher particle velocities with optimal spray distances.
generation.boundary: This intervention should remain effective for FeCoNiCrAl bond coats deposited onto substrates with as small as 120 mm internal diameters under high-temperature service conditions; its effectiveness for other compositions or radically different torch designs is not established.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvements in coating thickness and deposition efficiency are uncertain without further experimentation, and the optimal tuning of other deposition parameters (e.g., gas flow rates, powder feed) alongside spray distance requires additional study.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct controlled depositions using the HVAF-i7 torch on substrates with a 120 mm internal diameter. Run three sets: one with the current standard spray distance (control), one with a reduced spray distance of 300 mm, and one with 350 mm. All other deposition parameters (composition, feedstock, gas flow, etc.) are held constant. Evaluate the resulting coatings by measuring thickness, adhesion strength, oxidation states, and microstructural quality.
measurements: Oxidation level (using XPS or spectroscopic analysis)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coatings deposited at the reduced spray distances (300–350 mm) do not exhibit a statistically significant increase in thickness and overall improved deposition characteristics (adhesion and reduced oxidation) compared to the control, then the hypothesis is considered falsified.
